justification: Changes which pages the section reader sends to the AI: contents pages are dropped. Sample of 41 active chapters (40 random + Hornsby residential, 2026-10-28): 19 pages skipped in 10 chapters, all contents / list of tables / list of figures, read one by one; Hornsby page 2 among them.

falsifiable_check.fails_when: a contents page is passed to the reader, or a rule page is skipped
falsifiable_check.observed_red: 2026-10-28: before the change contents_pages did not exist and Hornsby page 2 was read, giving 80 not_found rules in the review run.

pre_impl.existing_data: Hornsby re-read 2026-10-27/28: 80 rules invented from the contents page (page 2), e.g. 'minimum 800 square metres' not in the PDF.
pre_impl.assumption_mismatch: The reader assumed every page holds content worth reading.
pre_impl.new_vs_existing: Reuses council_quote.contents_kind (merged #1530) per page; no new detector.

functions.name: contents_pages
functions.input: the chapter's (page, line text) pairs in reading order
functions.output: set of pages whose lines read as a contents list
functions.if_none: no lines gives an empty set, so nothing is skipped

values.if_missing: an empty page is never a contents page and is read as before

break_it.scenario: A page of numbered controls is mistaken for contents.
break_it.what_happens: Real rules on that page would never be read.
break_it.how: contents_kind refuses lines with rule wording or values, and needs 5+ lines; 41-chapter sample skipped 0 rule pages; the coverage/loss guard still flags lost rule lines.

break_it.scenario: A contents page is also flagged as a picture page.
break_it.what_happens: The vision reader could still invent rules from it.
break_it.how: Skipped pages are removed from the picture-page list too.

break_it.scenario: A contents page uses a layout the detector does not know.
break_it.what_happens: The reader still reads it and may invent rules, as before.
break_it.how: No worse than today; council_quote then marks contents text not_a_control (#1530) so it is never served.

post_merge.db_reset: No. Applies to the next re-read of any chapter.
